alignments.note: The lamed of the superscription is rendered For.
The article assimilated into the pointed preposition is a real token (rule 12) and takes the ASV the.
Piel participle of nṣḥ = one who directs; Chief carries the lexeme of overseeing and Musician is the specifier the ASV supplies (rules 24, 31). Heading on Musician remains defensible.
The Hebrew superscription is only lamnaṣṣēaḥ ləḏāwiḏ; no mizmôr stands here, so the italicized A Psalm is licensed by no morpheme (rules 7, 30).
The lamed of authorship/dedication is rendered of.
Proper name.
The perfect takes its English auxiliary; the explicit subject noun is its own unit (rule 17).
The anarthrous substantival adjective licenses the determiner the ASV supplies (rules 15, 29 spirit); it is not added.
Prefixed preposition.
Host noun without its suffix.
The pronominal suffix takes the possessive (rule 18); reordered target token.
The negative existential supplies the whole frame There is no, headed on the negation that carries its lexeme (rules 21, 24).
Subject of the verbless negative clause.
The ASV renders the hiphil with a copular predicate; subject pronoun and copula belong to the verb's unit, headed on the lexical predicate corrupt.
The hiphil of tʿb is the abominable acting itself, so abominable carries the lexeme while have done is the English periphrasis; heading on done remains defensible.
The accusative noun ʿălîlāh is rendered works.
The second negative existential is separately rendered There is none, parallel to the first occurrence; not a case for rule 22 since the ASV renders it.
The relative that the ASV supplies for the substantival participle belongs to it.
The ASV renders the participial construct with a direct object rather than of, so this unit takes only good (rule 28 spirit).

review_notes: Ledger checked: all 18 source IDs and all 33 target IDs are partitioned exactly once across 19 units; no invented IDs.
Accepted alignment judged correct and returned unchanged; only note wording was tightened with rule citations.

s003: kept Chief as target head because נצח supplies the directing/preeminence sense while Musician is the noun the ASV supplies; a reader preferring the substantive Musician has a defensible alternative, hence medium confidence.
s005/t005-t006: the italic A Psalm is genuinely unlicensed here (no מִזְמוֹר in this superscription), so the italic markup and the added label agree; this is not a case of rule 7 overriding markup.
s007: The before fool is a supplied determiner attached to the noun that licenses it, not an added unit; contrast rule 12, where a real [הַ] token exists in the superscription.
s014: alternative head done (English lexical verb) versus abominable (Hebrew lexeme of תעב) — retained abominable per rule 24's lexeme-first criterion, flagged medium.

alignments.note: Divine name rendered Jehovah.
Hiphil of שׁקף; the ASV renders the single verb as looked down, so both English tokens share the unit and the finite lexical verb heads it.
Prefixed preposition מִן → from.
heaven.
עַל → upon.
בְּנֵי is construct and carries no article token; the supplied English the belongs to this noun's unit (rules 15, 29).
Nomen rectum of the construct chain takes the English of (rule 19).
The לְ of the infinitive construct is here actually rendered, as To; rule 27 concerns לֵאמֹר, where it is not.
Infinitive construct רְאוֹת → see.
The interrogative הֲ under an indirect question surfaces as if; reading הֲיֵשׁ as one fused unit headed on יֵשׁ remains defensible.
Existential יֵשׁ takes the dummy subject there with its supplied copula (rule 21); heading on there instead of were is the competing analysis.
The substantival participle is expanded as any that did understand, headed on the word carrying the lexeme; any could alternatively be read as the predicate of יֵשׁ and joined to s011.
Substantival participle rendered That did seek after; after is taken as part of the English phrasal rendering of דרשׁ rather than as a realization of אֵת.
Object marker with no English realization (rule 16); the competing analysis attaches after (t023) to it.
אֱלֹהִים → God.

review_notes: Reviewed and left unchanged: every s### and t### is partitioned exactly once, all statuses have well-formed heads, and no unit merges morphemes that license separate English.

Checked the three points where the ledger could plausibly differ: (a) t016 any as predicate of יֵשׁ rather than part of the expanded participle, (b) t023 after as a realization of אֵת rather than of the phrasal seek after, (c) הֲיֵשׁ read as one fused interrogative-existential unit. Each is flagged medium in situ; the accepted analysis keeps the smaller defensible units and is retained.
Heads verified independently of unit edges per rule 24: looked over down, children over the, men over of, understand over any/that/did, seek over That/did/after.
s006 takes the supplied the without an article token because a construct noun cannot be articular (rules 15, 29); no added unit is warranted here.
s008 is aligned rather than unrepresented: unlike לֵאמֹר, this infinitival לְ is actually realized by To.

alignments.note: The article in הַכֹּל has no English 'the' and is therefore unrepresented under rule 12.
Substantival כֹּל is realized discontinuously as 'They ... all'; 'all' carries the lexeme.
סָר is rendered 'are gone aside'; the lexical predicate 'gone' is the target head.
יַחְדָּו is directly rendered 'together'.
The inflected plural verb supplies 'they are ... become filthy'; 'filthy' most directly realizes the Hebrew verbal lexeme.
Negative existential אֵין is rendered 'There is none', including the dummy subject and copula; 'none' realizes its negative-existential force.
The participle עֹשֵׂה is rendered by the relative construction 'that doeth'.
טוֹב is directly rendered 'good'.

The negative existential and scalar גַּם are jointly realized by the ASV's emphatic phrase 'no, not'. Neither assigning 'not' atomically to גַּם nor assigning both negatives solely to אֵין captures the correspondence as well.
אֶחָד is directly rendered 'one'.

review_notes: Corrected the closing clause by treating אֵין גַּם and the emphatic ASV rendering 'no, not' as one phrase-level alignment. The accepted analysis left גַּם unrepresented even though the English negative repetition conveys its scalar emphasis.
Kept the article s001 unrepresented because the ASV has no corresponding 'the'; the discontinuous 'They ... all' belongs to substantival כֹּל.
The interleaved target units in the first two clauses were retained without absorbing unrelated intervening tokens.

alignments.note: The interrogative particle is realized by the fronted auxiliary of the ASV question; alternatively 'Have' could be folded into the verb unit with the particle left unrepresented.
The finite verb 'do they know' is rendered by the noun of the light-verb phrase 'have no knowledge'.
The substantival participle takes the supplied 'the'; no Hebrew article is present, so the determiner belongs to the noun that licenses it.
Nomen rectum carries the English 'of'.
The participle is rendered as a relative clause, so 'Who eat up' is one unit.
The italic 'as' is the comparative link the ASV supplies for the juxtaposed clause; it could also be read as an addition licensed by no morpheme.
The Hebrew line is asyndetic; no waw stands before לֹא קָרָאוּ.
The verb governs its object directly in Hebrew, so the supplied 'upon' belongs to the verb.

The ASV recasts the cognate-accusative clause, so the finite verb surfaces only as the copula plus subject pronoun 'were they'; taking the whole 'were they in great fear' as one verbal unit is also defensible.
The cognate accusative is rendered as an adverbial phrase; 'in' is licensed by the accusative's function (rule 33) and 'great' is the intensity the cognate construction carries, so neither is added.
Verbless clause: the supplied copula 'is' belongs to the prepositional predicate that licenses it (rule 20).
Construct noun cannot take the article, so the English 'the' is supplied with the noun (rule 29).
The 'of' of the construct chain belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19), and the substantival adjective takes its supplied 'the'.
Hiphil of בּוֹשׁ with its subject pronoun; headed on shame, which carries the lexeme, rather than on the light verb put.
Construct noun cannot take the article, so the supplied the joins its own unit.
Nomen rectum takes of; the substantival adjective also licenses the.
Verbless clause: the supplied copula belongs to the predicate noun.

מִי יִתֵּן is a fixed optative idiom (rule 30); the ASV renders it with the discontinuous frame Oh that ... were come, so the interrogative and the verb share one unit headed on the English predicate.
מִן is realized by the fused English preposition out of.
A construct noun cannot take the article, so the supplied the belongs to this noun's unit (rule 29).
Nomen rectum carries the English of (rule 19).
בְּ with the infinitive construct is rendered temporally as When.
שׁוּב rendered as the phrasal verb bringeth back.
Supplied the belongs to the construct noun (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the English of; the possessive his is the suffix's own unit.
The Hebrew clause is asyndetic; Then is an English discourse connective no morpheme licenses.

The ASV swaps the two verbs lexically (גִּיל rendered rejoice, שָׂמַח rendered be glad); alignment follows each verb's own subject, so יָגֵל takes the predicate of Jacob. Auxiliary shall belongs to the verb (rule 17).
No waw stands before יִשְׂמַח; the ASV marks and as supplied.
Paired with the ASV's second predicate by subject, mirroring s013; the lexical anchor is glad.
